document:
Remove MPs 'special' income tax exemption for accommodation expenses, MPs advocate fairness, so should experience fairness in the tax system.
 
MPs have an exemption from the rules applied to other taxpayers by Income Tax (Earnings & Pensions) 2003 Sections 292, I believe their 'special' treatment is unfair treatment and should end.
 
Government and Treasury statements on IR35 Off-Payroll, repeated by Ministers and MPs in response to constituents questions, have made it clear that equal and fair tax treatment is appropriate and necessary. Further it has widespread support in the House of Commons
 
Two workers in the same situation, e.g. working away from home during the week, in Westminster should receive the same tax and expenses treatment.
 
Ensure that two workers whose work necessarily requires them to be at a location, e.g. Westminster, are treated identically. MPs should not be subject to different rules in ITEPA 2003 s292.
 
Make the Tax system equitable and fair.

Subject the Child Maintenance Service to review and ensure it's fit for purpose, To review how the Child Maintenance Service operates, to:
 
1) ensure transparency, consistency and clarity when assisting callers;
2) ensure that ALL incomes from the paying parent are taken into consideration from the outset of claims, and
3) speed up the mechanisms to enforce payment., The charity Gingerbread states that around a fifth of families with children in the UK are single parent. When separated parents disagree over Child Maintenance, payment must be claimed through the Child Maintenance Service. But this service is not fit for purpose and is letting children (living in single parent families) down across the UK. The inefficiency of this service is one of the key contributors to half of single parent families (49%) living in poverty, despite the fact that 69% of single parents work.

Introduce a minimum Wage (fee) for Gig-Economy Workers, With over 4.7 million people working in the gig-economy, there needs to be fair legislation set with minimum hourly earnings and allowance to holiday or sickness. That is one in ten adults working in the uk are unprotected and unpaid for holidays. Companies treat workers as that a worker!, Introduce legislation to force companies to pay a minimum hourly service rate, and holiday and sickness pay based upon hours worked each week/Earnings average. This is aimed at the likes of Uber, Deliveroo, JustEat & Amazon.

Include self-employed in statutory sick pay during Coronavirus, 4.8 million people are registered self-employed in the UK. Figures are of 2017 according to the Office of National Statisticics. It would be easy enough to work out what each person is entitled to based on their tax returns.
Include self-employed in statutory sick pay., The self-employed make up 15% of UK's workforce. Majority are not entitled to any sick pay. I want the Government to include us in the recent changes to statutory sick pay because of the Corona19 virus. Excluding us means the Government are running the risk of said people continuing going to work as just like everyone else we have bills to pay and thus spreading the virus.

Require employers to pay workers on a weekly basis., Many individuals find it difficult to budget for an entire month for themselves and their families for various reasons, for example: they've changed jobs, started receiving pension payments, or exited the Benefits system. It should be required that employers in the UK pay workers every 7 days., If the Government mandates that anyone who employs another person ensures they receive their payments on a weekly basis, people will be kept away from the State-provided benefits and assistance systems. This would be beneficial for both the Government, and the British people and help to ensure a fairer and more balanced United Kingdom.

Close Schools/Colleges down for an appropriate amount of time amidst COVID19., We would like the government to at least consider closing schools/colleges down in the coming weeks or as soon as possible, in addition to taking necessary actions to prevent further spread., We would like the Government or Parliament to enforce this action due to the growing fear among parents and students that attend school. The ability to focus or concentrate is affected in addition to the growing fears of the Corona-virus. In our view, the government and health officials around the world are more 'reactive' rather than 'proactive'. This will result in more spread as time is given for the virus to do so. We hope to come to an agreement as soon as possible in a timely manner.

Free transport for post 16 in  And at any further education, As all post 16 are to stay in education, then their travel to their nearest college/school which offer the courses/ education required to further their future should be free or at least heavily subsidised. 
Not all schools/colleges offer the same subjects which discriminates against the child., It appears unfair and discriminates children. If they are required to stay on in education, then their subject choices should be facilitated equally across the board .

Reform child maintenance and benefit calculations to be fair and prevent poverty, Make the system fair. If the receiving parent is on benefits then those should be reduced by the amount received in child maintenance. , The income used to calculate the  child maintenance rate of the paying parent should be net of taxes, NI and rent. The paying parent's children shouldn’t get less than the receiving parent's.

The current system is putting children in poverty. It is punishing working parents and rewarding those on benefits.

Close universities down for an appropriate amount of time amidst COVID19., Please close the universities across the UK for an appropriate amount of time to stop the spread of COVID-19., We would like the Government or Parliament to enforce this action due to the growing fear among parents and students that attend school. The ability to focus or concentrate is affected in addition to the growing fears of the Coronavirus. In our view, the government and health officials around the world are more 'reactive' rather than 'proactive'. This will result in more spread as time is given for the virus to do so. We hope to come to an agreement as soon as possible in a timely manner.

Make employers give a minimum number of hours to staff on Zero-hours contracts, Legislation should be introduced to require employers using ZHCs to notify their staff (after perhaps an initial trial period) of a minimum number of hours work a month in advance., This would make it easier for workers claiming Universal Credit to plan for changes in their income, as it only adjusts after a month.

ZHCs have been rising incredibly since 2010. They give flexibility to Employers and thus may be a good source of new employment, and they do suit some Employees.
 
However they can also cause people employed under them difficulties, and can contribute to people falling into arrears on Universal Credit (UC) because it only reacts to changes in hours a month later, and thus some employed in ZHC may be on insufficient hours to make ends meet.
 
Further information supporting this petition is available here: http://bit.ly/2TIhyTe

Cancel Belfast St. Patrick's Day due to coronavirus risk, We would like the Government or Parliament to enforce this action due to the growing fear among community. The ability to focus or concentrate is affected in addition to the growing fears of the Corona-virus., In our view, the government and health officials around the world are more 'reactive' rather than 'proactive'. We would like the government to force councils to cancel St. Patrick's Day celebrations in the coming weeks or as soon as possible, in addition to taking necessary actions to prevent further spread.

Review drink spiking and bring in provisions to protect people from spiking, The Government should look into drink spiking, the facts and figures behind it, and review the way we deal with victims who believe they have been spiked. , The Government should require bars, clubs and pubs to take greater precautions in order to prevent it, and put in place arrangements to provide after care for those who have been spiked.

I was spiked last month and I was shocked at how little is in place to: one protect victims, but also to deal with the crime itself.
 
Figures show that last year reports of drink spiking hit a 5 year high, and the issue continues to grow.
 
There is not enough advice online on what to do if you find yourself in this situation. Crimes are going unreported, and people feel unsafe.
 
Testing is difficult to access, and the police may not investigate without it. It's time for change.

Protect benefits claimants from sanctions for missed appointments during COVID19, We need the Government to guarantee that no one will be sanctioned for missing appointments for Universal Credit or any other out of or in work benefits during Coronavirus., Social distancing is essential to limiting the spread of Coronavirus. People on benefits need assurances that they will not be sanctioned for missing appointments during Coronavirus, otherwise people with the virus may be tempted to travel to appointments, placing other people at risk from infection.

Force councils to repair potholes faster & get claims for damages paid quicker, I damaged the front wheel of my car after hitting a pothole in the middle nowhere late at night (I'm female) I'm on low income and need my car for work. I'm frustrated with Lincolnshire council for lack of road maintenance and lack of care to the public, the time it takes for a claim to processed, The Government must force councils to prioritize to fix potholes in a reasonable time. We MOT our cars to make them fit for the roads, why can't we MOT the roads so they are fit for the cars. better quality repairs not just filled with tarmac. time from reporting a pothole to repair needs to be quicker (less paperwork)

Remove Universal Credit's 'Minimum Income Floor' for the self-employed., I want Parliament and the Government to address the flaws within Universal Credit such as the Minimum Income Floor and to address the impact this is having on the self-employed., Nearly a sixth of the UK’s workforce is self-employed. The Minimum Income Floor continues to punish the self-employed who have fluctuating monthly income and runs completely contrary to the Government’s own stated aims of ‘making work pay’ under UC.

The self-employed may be thousands of pounds worse-off each year under Universal Credit compared to employees outside of UC who are making similar amounts. 

This is not fair. This is discriminatory. Please address this before more damage is done.

Give financial help to agency and zero hour workers during COVID-19 outbreak., Put in place an emergency fund for people who work for agencies, are on zero hour contracts, or who are self employed and may not be able to claim Universal Credit should work dry up due due to emergency measures during the outbreak of COVID 19., Many families may be forced into hardship and debt if the bread winners lose out on work due to school closures or big event cancellations. Whilst some may be eligible for Universal Credit other may not be but still rely on the income to look after their families. Not knowing if they are going to be able to put food on the table is an added stress which may impinge on mental health and the spread of the virus.

Stop using student finance loans as an income when claiming universal credit, Take off student finance and loans as an income when claiming universal credit.  This is a loan which students have to pay back once studies have finished and working so students are paying twice for their studies when it is taken as an income for claiming universal credit, Why should University students be punished twice for studying and bettering themselves for their careers?  Student finance and loans are exactly what it states and should not be classed as an income when they have to pay all this back. It is hard enough that universal credit is poor then having money deducted for having student loans.

For the Government to legislate to abolish the Benefits Cap., To introduce legislation that removes the Benefits Cap., The Benefits Cap was brought in during the discredited era of austerity, where it was wrongly stated that people on benefits were receiving far more than people in employment.  This was never the reality for the majority. The Benefits Cap is an existing relic of a failed agenda which is having a detrimental effect on the lives of those in receipt of benefits.

Businesses to work from home for an appropriate amount of time amidst COVID19, We would like the government to at least consider closing down offices/businesses and order to work from home as soon as possible, in addition to taking necessary actions to prevent further spread. This will prevent the spread during the commutes and meetings., We would like the Government or Parliament to enforce this action due to the growing fear among workers. The ability to focus or concentrate is affected in addition to the growing fears of the Corona-virus. In our view, the government and health officials around the world are more 'reactive' rather than 'proactive'. This will result in more spread as time is given for the virus to do so. We hope to come to an agreement as soon as possible in a timely manner.
Sick pay for self employed Carers, Self employed Carers should be paid if they have to take time off for sick leave.,

Self employed people should be entitled to SSP and Paternal Leave, Self employed people are hard working and pay their own taxes and NI but they are not entitled to any sick pay or paternity leave. 
I don't think this is fair and it seems to be discriminatory as most of the times they work harder that employed people., Parliament to take in to consideration how hard self employed people work and change the system so they get SSP and paternity leave as any other workers. This should be basic rights for anyone contributing to the tax system.

Give all an income if schools, workplaces shut during COVID19/Coronavirus scare, Give adults a basic income of £1500 per month of shutdown and give them £500 for each of their dependent children.  This could be done via employer's payrolls and also direct to bank accounts of child benefit claimants.  For the self employed it could be done via self-assessment., A good government has a duty to its citizens during an unprecedented time like this.  Many people do not have the means to provide for themselves without regular income.  They do not have the savings to survive even a month if their workplace closes or if they have to stop work to provide childcare.  People have been paying taxes to the government for years and now expect the government to provide the safety net it needs.

Stop Universal Credit make deductions from benefits for student loans, Stop Universal Credit make deductions from benefits for student loans. It is a loan we need to pay off not a salary or benefit. We are being robbed for our money we are entitled to by law., It is effecting peoples and families mental and emotional health. Its is making us financially vulnerable to Support our children and families. Students have discussed this on a daily basis. It is not only effecting adults but also children. It is causing alarm and distress to people and we need the government to stop robbing us for our money we are entitled to. It is a LOAN not a salary or income, we will eventually have to pay it back, so realistically the government is taking away our money

Provide financial support to performers and creators during the COVID-19 crisis, The prospect of widespread cancellations of concerts, theatre productions and exhibitions due to COVID-19 threatens to cause huge financial hardship for Britain's creative community. We ask Parliament to provide a package of emergency financial and practical support during this unpredictable time., Only government can compensate individual performers and creators for lost work, and provide emergency funding to orchestras, venues, theatres and festivals. Extensive cancellations, downturns in attendance and earned income, and loss of opportunity threaten the viability of hundreds of organisations and the livelihood of thousands of artists. Immediate and robust action is urgently needed to ensure that Britain remains a world leader in the creative industries.

Divide Child Benefit equally between separated parents who share equal care., If children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent, the Child Benefit should be split equally between both parents., Child Benefit is currently only paid to one parent by HMRC.
 
Currently, if parents of a child are separated, and the child spends equal time with both parents, only parent can receive Child Benefit, and receives the full amount. This can mean one parent, who earns significantly more than the other, can receive the full Child Benefit while the other parent receives nothing.
 
This is incredibly outdated in this age modern parenting and inclusivity for all.

Amend the IR35 Reforms to re-instate the 5% allowance for all contractors, Tax avoidance schemes are a real threat to UK taxpayers who unwittingly use a scheme provider, believing it to be an employment intermediary, as could happen following a ban on PSCs by many hirers., HMRC must disrupt the activities of scheme providers using any means at the department's disposal.
 
The government should protect taxpayers from any risk of involvement in tax avoidance schemes, in order to avoid tax debts and a loss of rights to contributory benefits.
 
Re-instating the 5% allowance under the off payroll working rules would reduce the incentive for non-compliance with the new rules, and thereby reduce opportunities for the involvement of potentially dangerous organisations in the labour supply chain.

Provide immediate financial support to the Tourism Industry., Immediate tangible financial support is required for many businesses and their staff in the Tourism Industry that are struggling with cash flow now, as a direct result of the virus. There is a swift requirement of cash injections into the industry to keep business's alive and staff employed., Tourism employs over 3 million people in this country, 10% of the total workforce and over £130 Billion of GDP. 
Tourism's impact on the economy is estimated by Deloitte's as having a GVA (Gross value added) multiplier to be 2.8 – meaning that for every £1,000 generated in direct tourism, there is a further £1,800 that is supported elsewhere in the economy through the supply chain and consumer spending. It is imperative that the government directly supports this sector with immediate action.

Offering financial aid for people losing hours and jobs due to Coronavirus., Help with financial aid for people losing hours and jobs due to the virus outbreak. People working in tourism, hospitality, retail and self employed sectors who are unable to work from home and who are not being financially supported through their businesses during this massive loss in revenue., Will help stop a financial crisis and a massive recession. Will support the public during a difficult time where families are already struggling. Sectors that people are unable to work from home should be supported by the employer or if not possible, the government.

Require courts to make an attachment of earnings order where a debt is owed, We want the government to require a court to make an attachment of earnings order when it rules that a debtor owes a person/business money. , The debt would automatically be paid back from future earnings made by the debtor at an affordable rate via the debtors NI number, making it easier for people to get back what is rightfully theirs.
The current situation makes it too difficult to get money back from a debtor and too easy for a debtor to evade paying back what they owe. If the situation was rectified hard working businesses and people that are owed money would rightfully get their money back and struggle less. The change would also serve as a much needed deterrent to people trying to avoid paying their debts. This change could boost the economy by keeping more businesses running and creating more taxable income.

Provide a loan facility for self employed workers and directors of companies, Provide a loan facility to self employed workers and directors of companies at the current Bank of England base rate for upto 1 year based upon an average weekly wage for the last 3 months for whatever time duration there is a lockdown in place over the COVID19 virus, This would help self employed workers with their outgoings during the COVID19 outbreak, who do not have savings and would be unable to work if a shutdown is implemented

Encourage banks to delay 40% bank overdraft charges during the corona pandemic, Self employed people and others may be severely impacted by work cancellations during the corona pandemic. In light of this, it could be very difficult to manage financially and going overdrawn may become unavoidable. To be hit with near 40% charges in the current climate is financially devastating., To introduce these new bank charges now, couldn't be worse timing. We want the government to work with banks to prevent people from being hampered by these new charges, during what are already very difficult and stressful times with employment and lack of it.
The British government should set a net migration cap at 10,000 a year., Net immigration should be reduced to 10,000 a year to take the pressure off the public services.,

Increase Statutory Sick Pay payments, Increase Statutory Sick Pay to be inline with the cost of living, I honestly find it insane that the government expects someone to live of £94.25 per week when someone could be earning working 40 hours a week earning £372 inline with the living wage then they could see their wage cut by almost £280 a week!

Require all private hospitals to treat Coronavirus patients, For the government to take immediate legal action to require private hospitals to requisition their beds and to treat the public during the coronavirus crisis, The electorate will expect the government to be able to mobilise all health capacity - be it public or private - to deal with what the Prime Minister has described as ‘the worst public health crisis for a generation’.  The private health sector cannot be excluded from this mobilisation.

We would like the government to consider social care as equally important to NHS, We would like the government to support and regard social care: financially, publicly and systematically on an equal par as NHS. We would like parliament to debate how to support social care during COVID-19 and beyond so that it automatically has the same access to operational and financial support., Practically, there is parity of position between health and social care: Social care employs more people than health, is intrinsically community based and supports a large number of the population. However, there is a significant lack of parity of esteem between the two. The government’s recent early response to the COVID-19 and the March 2020 budget was exemplary of this lack of parity. This includes the pay and rewards of staff, professionalisation, funding, training and political discourse.

If UK schools close, provide food vouchers for children on free school meals, If the UK schools have to close due to coronavirus, I propose that all families of children who receive free school meals are issued with food/shopping vouchers in order to ensure that they have enough food and other essentials to see them through., I work in a school with a high proportion of low income families and I am genuinely worried about how they will feed their families if the schools close. The food banks will help, but there will be nowhere near enough to help all those who need it. These families will not have budgeted for this and will certainly struggle, as will a lot of families.

Covid-19 economic support by Government for workers in The Arts & Entertainment, For the UK government to provide economic assistance to people who work in the arts and entertainment industry.

The UK has thousands of people suffering unforeseen financial challenges that could have a profound effect on hundreds of thousands of people employed in the sector., When people think of arts they think big names however there are tens of thousands of people who today find themselves with no work because of Covid.

They have had concerts, theatre shows, art sales cancelled for completely understandable safety reasons.

But many of these people live on the gig to gig basis.

The government needs to help these people and prevent people losing their home, their car, their livelihood.

Without art and culture we are less. Lets support these who lift us up

Increase the amount of statuary sickness to allow people to survive., 118£ a week are not enough for people to survive. During this pandemic many people are obliged to be off work and will fall into poverty. Provide the necessary help for people to survive., Increase the statuary sickness or implement a plan to offer a sustainable support to the population that will fall into poverty due to loss of work, or that will not perceive a salary during the pandemic.

Abolish the changes to IR35 implented in April 2020, Because this will massively affect the economy due to the Corona virus and especially the contractors' life., Because this is not fair to pay the same tax with permanent employee and not take the same benefits like holiday pay,sick pay or when the companies cancel with sort notice.also,we pay as well and NI of the employer when we use an umbrella company

Prevent banks charging  fees for card payments to small businesses, With the need for people to avoid contamination during the current pandemic, going cashless could reduce germs being spread. However, many small businesses have to pay to take card payments. Lifting this fee would enable people to reduce handling cash without creating costs for small businesses.,

Fund free meals for NHS staff whilst on duty during the COVID19 Pandemic, Provide NHS staff free meals by way of hospital catering or meal vouchers during the COVID19 Pandemic period. This will boost morale and ensure staff are reenergised through their work day., NHS staff are going to be under increased demand and pressure during the COVID19 Pandemic. It is important that they are looked after during their demanding shifts.

I believe the government should provide free meals by the way of vouchers or using caterers during this period. 

Staff are likely to be volunteering to complete longer shifts or additional days to cope with the demand. They need to be replenished and this would be the right way to do it.

Trial Univeral Basic Income from now until COVID-19 is over., Start a trial of Universal Basic Income now and continue it until the end of the COVID-19 outbreak at least. It will be easier than dealing with the enormous amount of sickness claims that will be submitted., I would like the government to pay anyone who applies a Universal Basic Income at a rate of £95.85 per week (same as Statutory Sick Pay starting 6th April). Payments should start as quickly as possible and be classed as income for tax & income-related benefit purposes. If the trial goes well then it could be expanded to replace all income-related benefits and eventually to all UK citizens instead of being stopped.

Close NI nurseries, schools and colleges with immediate effect due to Covid-19, Protect the Safety and Rights of those who WORK in and ATTEND schools in line with our counterparts in the South.
Lack of clarity and guidance from leadership above school level has left us vulnerable and compromised.
Our schools are unable to follow current guidance from the Public Health Agency., We don't have the luxury of  being able able to have our children sit one metre apart.Many of our schools are unable to follow the handwashing protocol as they don't have warm water! 
We NEED to be afforded the same  consideration as our schools and colleges in the South of Ireland. 
I ask you, WHO has made the determination that the Lives of children and staff are LESS VALUABLE in the North than those of the chidren and staff in the South!
I urge you please to sign this petition.

Ban or limit bailouts for big businesses, Too many big businesses rely on the Government when they are in financial difficulty, and all too often the Government provides financial support. It has to stop. The Government should let businesses fail rather than bail them out., The Government should ban or at least put a cap on how much financial support the Government can provide to companies in financial difficulty. This money should go to funding public services, not supporting large companies. During the current outbreak public services are more important than ever, and should take priority over support for private businesses.

Set up a COVID-19 hardship fund for small businesses/individuals, Set up a hardship fund to support small businesses/individuals affected by COVID-19. Allow taxpayers to make voluntary payments to the fund., Many small businesses, self-employed workers and families are very worried about the economic impact of COVID-19 and I believe many people would be willing to make voluntary contributions (however small) so that they can receive financial assistance during the coming months.

Government needs to increase the wages of retail/food employees due to Covid 19, Financial support to be offered to food and shop workers in the UK in order to keep this vital service operational, These people are putting their health at risk for minimum wage in order to provide vital services during covid 19 outbreak.

Help sole traders: postpone interim tax payments due July 2020, to Jan 2021., Sole traders & small businesses need financial help in light of Covid-19 challenges. Postpone the interim tax payments due in July 2020, to Jan 2021. Small business already income is dropping off. Many businesses will re-build after we emerge from these difficult times but will need Government help., Small businesses and some traders don’t benefit from statutory sick pay or business rate waivers, or any other forms of financial help that the Government has so far muted.

Suspend temporary the commissions taken by app based ride hailing companies., Suspend temporary the commissions taken by app based ride hailing companies such as UBER, Bolt, etc, to minimalise the loss of earnings for workers as most of them are self employed. The service provided by these app are probably the safest., Suspend temporary the commissions taken by app based ride hailing companies such as UBER, Bolt, etc, to minimalise the loss of earnings for workers as most of them are self employed. The service provided by these apps are probably the safest right now as we can minimalise the social contact. Saving the workers those commissions they loose less income during the very insecure period of time they face due to the Coronavirus Pandemic.

Immediate UK government ordered closure for all entertainment and social spaces, Issue an immediate and direct UK wide closure order to all theatres, music venues, pubs, nightclubs and other entertainment spaces considered to be a mass gathering space as defined by the government., Entertainment spaces across the UK are not currently entitled to any claim covering revenue lost throughout the Covid-19 crisis. This is because the current directive is only a recommendation to the public, which whilst remaining solely as a recommendation is not covered for loss of earnings by insurance. Tens of thousands of people working within these sectors are now at significant risk of the industry financially collapsing without immediate government intervention to rectify this.

Bail out the People before Big Business, The Covid-19 Pandemic is going to cause our society untold hardship. We will all need help. European governments are putting their people before big business - offering full financial support to everyone, as soon as they need it, for as long as it takes. Our Government should put people first too., We live in a consumer society. The economy is entirely driven by people having money to spend. If people don't have money to spend, everything stops. Give the people the money today to keep the economy going and it will cheaper than restarting when it's all over.

Shut down hospitality sector during COVID19 + relief packages for small business, The government should mandate the closure of restaurants and other aspects of the hospitality industry during COVID-19 in order to protect citizens and slow the spread of the virus. In addition, the government should provide relief packages to owners of small businesses within this sector., The hospitality industry is the third largest economy in the UK. Three million jobs are at risk and we need the government to provide relief packages to small businesses so that members of the hospitality sector do not go out of business. Since members of the public are no longer advised to leave their homes unless necessary, it is surely no longer advisable for members of the hospitality to keep providing these services.

Give the entertainment and leisure industry official instruction to close, Give the entertainment and leisure industry official instruction to close premises so they can secure compensation and insurances, Without this instruction, and with advice not to attend venues, the industry will collapse with no income and hundreds of thousands of people are at risk of unemployment in the immediate future.

Government assurance to those that are self-employed, Due to the current coronavirus pandemic, those that are self-employed are going to be significantly adversely affected by a lack of work due to cancelled events as a result of the outbreak. This can mean a huge proportion of self-employed people will potentially go without money for the foreseeable, If the self-employed are to go months without earning money, some of the businesses and companies they work for could go under, meaning that even when the coronavirus pandemic is over, the work might not be there to resume. The government must thus provide economic assurance to each person self-employed in the UK in light of this situation. This could be through suspending things such as mortgage payments, providing financial relief in form of grants, or through pumping money into needed sectors

Implement Basic Universal Income for all citizens over 16, with N.I number., Immediately pass emergency legislation that creates Basic Universal Income for all. Paid by bank transfer monthly, to all with NI Number & bank account. Amount should reflect cost of living and rent / mortgage payments, i,e £1,500 per month and paid without condition of circumstance., We are in an unprecedented crisis, both medically & commercially. The consequences for all are far reaching; most people face immediate economic hardship. Basic Universal Income ensures business & self employed survive the current conditions & our economic landscape will not be so damaged. Workers facing long unemployment & self isolation will be able to pay rent & feed families, along with other vulnerable groups in the UK. 
DWP should be overhauled, with BUI replacing state pension & benefits.

Set up a Covid19 Emergency payment and Covid19 unemployment payment ., Set up an emergency payment and speedy unemployment benefit for those whose employment or self employment is adversely affected due to Covid19. Payments which are specifically designed to get thousands of people into payment as quickly as possible., Many people's work and self employment will be affected by Covid 19, either due to risk of contracting the virus or economic downturn. Whilst mortgages can be deferred, those who rent will be at greater risk of losing their homes, and bill's still need to be paid by all. It isn't just big businesses that need a helping hand. Many self employed people are at risk of losing their livelihood and employed people cannot afford to take unpaid leave. We need an emergency benefit such as Ireland have.

Allow full time students to claim universal credit during the Covid-19 pandemic, Currently most full time students are not eligible to claim for universal credit. Many work in the hospitality industry to support themselves and families.  The government should lift the restrictions on who is eligible to claim universal credit during this global crisis., Measures have been put in place to support all workers but not students. Many have families and accommodation to pay for and may face the choice of dropping out to be able to claim benefits.

Use  money from the foreign aid budget to Support UK in the Covid 19 crisis, Use some of the money set aside for foreign aid to assist with supporting our own country through the corona virus pandemic crises, Its is quite clear that this coronavirus pandemic is going to cost the country many billions of pounds to deal with and compensate for, and there is every chance that it will go on for years. we as a country will be putting less and less tax into the system as more and more workers are laid off, and support is given to the low paid and self employed. We have billions of pounds ringfenced to support countriesthat may end up supporting us!!!! use it for this country,

UK government to suspend all local council tax during the Covid19 crisis, UK government to suspend all local council tax during the Covid19 crisis to give UK nationals some financial relief during this unprecedented time., UK government to suspend all local council tax during the Covid19 crisis to give UK nationals some financial relief during this unprecedented time. UK government to make up the shortfall to local councils budgets by accessing emergency funding aid and providing this too local councils.
financial support hospitality industry to avoid job losses, Support Financially hospitality industry during this unprecedented times, Inject cash into hotel businesses so there are no job losses

Remove Congestion Charge and ULEZ during COVID-19 crisis, Amid the current COVID crisis, self employed workers suffer the most as no statutory pay is in place, including PCO and chauffeur drivers. They have to pay Congestion Charge and ULEZ daily. I urge for a suspension of these charges as work is scarce and paying these charges is unfair at this time., They are self employed and are already suffering the greatest damage to earnings amid this crisis. Work is minimal as people are encouraged to follow self-isolation procedures. Drivers are out all day with no jobs and still have to pay fines. If statutory pay does not apply to self-employed drivers, the least that can be done is to suspend charges.

Incentivise NHS staff during the COVID19 outbreak by making wages untaxable, In a struggling health care system, the country's population are relying on the NHS to maintain normal work despite pressures that are growing. I propose that the government make any health care and social care hours worked untaxable. Allow people with PAYE earnings for 2019-2020 to claim from HMRC under CJRS., Employees can be denied CJRS without reason or recourse as implementation is at the discretion of employers. Extend the furlough scheme for high-risk people who can't safely return to work., We call on the Government to keep furlough going beyond August for those who are shielding or high-risk and cannot safely return to work. Clarity on government scrapping immigration health surcharge for NHS workers., Following the government announcement on May the 21st, we as ACMA Southern Doctor's Network demand a clear detailed outline of when changes will take effect, how those who paid the fee since the announcement will be reimbursed and when; and if NHS workers' dependants and spouses will be exempt, It has been well over a month since the announcement and to date NHS workers are still paying the surcharge. Increase VAT threshold from £85,000 to £200,000 for restaurant sector, Of the small restaurants that are now trying to open, many are in a turnover bracket of £85,000 to £200,000. Extension of current Help to Buy Equity Loan by a Year., Help to buy has helped a lot of people climb on the property ladder. Extend the furlough scheme at 80% until at least December 2020, Extend the furlough scheme at 80% for businesses who due to the covid19 pandemic are unable to operate or have limited capacity to operate and generate income due to the covid19 pandemic. Such as Hospitality, weddings, opticians, entertainment, health and beauty, travel and tourism., If the furlough scheme is not extended at 80% until at least December 2020 many businesses will have no choice but to make redundancies to keep from folding, which could lead to thousands possibly millions being unemployed and causing further economical damage as people will be unable to pay for basic necessities such as food and housing. This will damage the economy further as no one will be spending and could lead to a job crisis and take the country much longer to recover and rebuild.

Extend the government furlough scheme to those working in the events sector., Though Parliament have announced a 1.75bn scheme to help the arts unfortunately this does not cover the entire sector. With the furlough scheme winding down in October, there should be a further extension to the furlough scheme available to those within the industry who cannot go back to work.,

Fund vouchers for high streets, hospitality & the arts to every adult & child, Funding a £500 voucher to every adult and a £250 voucher to every child could help safeguard millions of jobs and provide our high streets, hospitality sector and the arts with the vital cash injection that is desperately needed to save businesses from collapse and prevent mass unemployment., Millions are out-of-work or in insecure jobs, struggling to feed and clothe their families and pay for basics. For hard-working, low-income families, a meal out is a luxury many can't afford - even at half-price. Rishi Sunak had a chance to level-up Britain by giving every household a voucher to spend that would bring welcome relief to all. Instead he created a gimmick that favours those with disposable income, and in doing so, left those hardest hit by the crisis out in the cold again.

Protect those excluded from Covid support from contributing to the cost, In the absence of any action by the Government to support all taxpayers equally and fairly during this crisis we demand that those tax payers excluded from support packages are also excluded from contributing to the bill for the support they have been excluded from., This situation has been recognised as unjust.  The Government are aware of the plight of this substantially large group and continue to refuse to support.  This is despite calls from a significant number of MP's and an All Party Parliamentary Group to do so.  Many small businesses are now failing, people are losing their homes, people cannot eat or heat their homes.  Significant mental health problems are now present within this group.  The Government are deliberately excluding this group from receiving the support offered to others and are acting in a discriminatory fashion.  It would be unfair to expect this group to contribute to theGovernments bill for doing so.

Remove all restrictions on amateur musicians, Professionals often accompany choral societies and supplement amateur orchestras. By keeping restrictions on amateur music the Government prevent professionals earning a living. Amateur players are no more likely to pass on Covid 19 than professionals. Music is good for improving mental Health., The recent guidance from DCMS is at best very confusing and at worst discriminatory. We want the Government to rewrite the guidance to include amateur musicians in exemptions. All musicians should be allowed to perform without restrictions. I am a professional flautist and there is a cross over between the two sectors as pros often accompany choral societies as previously stated. I have also had professional engagements playing concertos with amateur orchestras.

Extend furlough scheme for the UK Aviation sector to help stop redundancies, We call on the Government to intervene and provide support to the UK Aviation Industry by increasing the furlough period as per other European countries. If Government support has been provided, any form of agreement should caveat that future dividend pay outs be paused until recovery is ensured., easyJet has

We emphasis the importance of protecting and maintaining regional connectivity. The Government must get a commitment from operators receiving financial assistance that they will continue to operate out of their current regional UK bases.

Give unpaid carers the recognition and financial reward they so justly deserve., To fully discuss the plight many carers find themselves in, through the lack of financial help and to give full recognition to unpaid carers through the media, Since 1976, when Carers Allowance was introduced, it has been paid at a percentage of long term contributory benefits, yet the value carers save the economy amounts to £Billions each year. With the extra pressure of Covid 19,  unpaid carers have simply been  let down.

Allow all employees access to references provided by past employers, Under the Data Protection Act individuals are not entitled to access a confidential employment reference written about them; either from the author of the reference i.e. the ex-employer, or from the recipient of the reference i.e. the new or prospective employer., This exemption to the right to access personal information could be in breach of Article 8 of the European Convention of Human Rights in respect of an individual’s right to a private life, as it is questionable whether the exemption which permits the reference to be withheld is proportionate to the individual’s right to fairness and transparency regarding their personal data.

Employ Newly Qualified Teachers to support schools., This years Newly Qualified Teachers have been faced with a lack of job vacancies across the country due to COVID-19. Why can’t we do the same?, By recruiting this years Newly Qualified Teachers in some capacity we could ensure that schools have extra support in September. Also we could ensure that this years cohort are not left seeking work in other areas and potentially lost to the profession. At a time when schools and learners are under much pressure to make up for learning disrupted by school closure, this years Newly Qualified Teachers could be used to deliver support such as targeted interventions.

To call on parliament to debate the bounceback loans farce, To call on the banks through parliament to sort out the bounceback loan farce where sole traders are not getting the vital help promised to us by the chancellor ., This is a national disgrace . Help promised by the chancellor has been denied to many sole traders , leaving many without a roof over their heads and in many cases driving people to the edge of suicide . This must stop now , the banks must be held to account by parliament to ensure that those of us who are sole traders are able to get this vital life line .

Fund free school meals for all students!, Let's work in ending bullying and stigmatisation when it comes to free school meals. This will bridge the inequality gap and strengthen inclusion in our schools. Social inequalities, racism, bullying, "affordability gap", attainment gap can be eradicated by offering all students free school meals., Debate about this must take place, it is needed now! A healthy meal is what a child needs and at school where they spend most of the day. The government must consider this asap to avoid kids being hungry.
There are multiple reasons why parents/carers cannot provide healthy meal at home: affordability, time constraints, health issues, etc.
Many school kids will go hungry in these unprecedented times. Furlough, businesses closing down, stress and mental health have risen. Matters are serious!

A government cash bailout for the coach industry before it's too late., Please help this sector with much needed money so we can keep these companies afloat.

We keep tens of thousands of people in jobs in our sector and hundreds of thousands of people in other industries.

Who takes kids to school?

We bring billions of pounds to the UK economy.

Reverse the decision to exclude Nursing staff from the public sector pay rise, Rishi Sunak announced today that Public sector workers are to receive a wage increase backdated due to the exceptional work that they have all carried out during the Covid-19 pandemic however, Nursing staff are to be excluded from this due to an pre-agreed pay increase structure from 2018., Mr Sunak MUST reverse his decision regarding the exclusion of Nursing staff from the salary increase as the 2018 agreed wage increase did not account for the emotional and physical distress that this pandemic has caused them. 
Excluding the backbone of our NHS from the salary increase is a deplorable decision and they should be rewarded for the extremely hard work that they have done. They have suffered from pay freezes, short staffing issues, extreme stress and lack of investment for so long.

Give ALL public sector workers an equal payrise, It has been announced today, that some public sector workers will receive a pay increase following their hard work during Covid 19. 
This is devastating news to many not included who continually feel disregarded by government.

Support the four pillar plan for recovery in the performing arts & entertainment, Government must implement the 4 pillar plan for recovery in the performing arts & entertainment:
1 Workforce Protection: financial help for all creative workers 
2 Safe Opening: including ticketing subsidies 
3 Protecting Infrastructure: beyond the mainstream arts
4 Equality: no one left behind, Creative workers, in their tens of thousands, lobbied for, and welcomed, the Government’s rescue package for the arts but it is becoming increasingly clear that the £1.57bn promised may not directly help them. 
Re-opening the sector is not enough. The reality of the phased return to work is that work opportunities will remain severely limited for tens of thousands of self-employed creatives. 
The performing arts and entertainment cannot recover without investment in both workplaces and workers.

Tax Break in pay for the NHS & Key workers who have worked during the lockdown, A tax break for all those key workers, supermarket, NHS and front-line staff who have been working durning the lockdown and keeping the UK running. Staff who have not been furloughed by their employer and have still been working during the pandemic should revive a tax break in their monthly pay., Those who have been furloughed by their employer have been getting their full pay (with governments help) and been spending time at home while those who are key workers, teachers and NHS have been keeping the UK running during the lockdown whilst getting abuse from the general public. A tax break in monthly pay for the months since lockdown was initiated for the work they have done to keep the UK afloat. A 6 month tax break for those who have worked as key workers during this time.

Recognise Unpaid Carers.A Fair amount reflecting the commitment & care provided, The UK Government to match the Scottish Supplementary payments (£230.10 Biannually) for unpaid Carer’s in England & Wales. It's unacceptable that any carer should suffer financially when providing such a valued service.Gov’t have to recognise the vital contribution & sacrifices they make daily.Without them full time paid care would have to be provided.

Fund free travel for Under 18s, Under 18s have free travel on TfL Services (excluding Trains, Thameslink etc.). As a young adult, I know how this’ll affect those around me. This is unjust and unfair, especially to those families claiming Universal Credit and other related benefits.

Ask the FCA to investigate banks for their handling of BBL applications, Parliament needs to ask the Financial Conduct Authority to investigate how banks have handled the application process for BBLs and why ‘feeder’ accounts that are open for a matter of hours to obtain funds are being credit checked when BBL’s themselves are not required to be credit checked, Businesses are being declined Bounce Back Loans due to credit checked being performed to open a feeder account and also the amount of time it takes them to process an application 

Some state it takes 6 days but there are concerns that some people are having to wait months.

Let Us Dance - Support nightclubs, dance music events and festivals, Extend funding to nightclubs, dance music events and festivals as part of the £1.57bn support package announced by the government for Britain's arts and culture sector to survive the hit from the pandemic. #LetUSDance, The government has failed to provide specific support to UK festivals, dance venues and nightclubs. Protect a percentage of jobs in the UK's offshore sector, In many offshore sectors around the world, their respective Governments protect a percentage of jobs for their own nationals. This is bad for our economy in tax revenue, VAT, and heightened redundancy levels

Stop the government taxing over 40s. Make them tax billionaires., The disparity in this is ridiculous. Some over 40s earn a lot less than some in their 20s and 30s. Women will be effected more so.. many jobs that women do part time do not pay over 18K. Billionaires evade tax, yet Gov.uk want to punish the poorest in society., Stop this from happening. Tax the rich who earn over a certain amount a year. Not by age. It’s retarded.

Remove national insurance and means test for ESA for disabled people, In order to get Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) you need to have paid enough national insurance credits or meet a means test.
, As someone who is chronically ill and disabled I have not been able to work enough hours to meet the national insurance requirement, and do not meet the means test.

The Government should remove the national insurance and means test for claiming ESA for chronically ill or disabled people, who should be able to claim this support when it is needed.
 
I worked part time even when struggling as I didn't want to rely on benefits, but now I need this support am not entitled to it.

Increase £30,000 redundancy pay tax free threshold to £60,000 or fully tax free., Currently up to £30,000 of redundancy pay is tax free. Given it is and will be a very difficult job market this threshold should be increased to £60,000 or made completely tax free., Given the current circumstances with COVID19 lot more people are going to lose their jobs relying completely on the redundancy money they will receive. It will take a lot longer for someone to find alternative employment and therefore this move will help all those individuals to live on the redundancy money for a little bit longer instead of making a claim for Unemployment benefits. This will also help their families and be able to cope for a few more months during these unpresidented times.

Change the criteria for SEISS grants for 2019-2020 tax year traders, Change the eligibility criteria for the second and third SEISS grants to include those who have traded and submitted a tax return for the tax year 2019-2020., The current eligibility criteria for the second SEISS grant does not include those who have traded and submitted a tax return for the 2019-20 tax year. This is unfair, as those who graduated in 2019 and have been trading for over a year are not currently entitled to the same support as those who graduated in 2018, despite working just as hard.

Include Solar PV and battery storage in the Greener Homes Grant, This would open up Solar PV and battery storage up to more households, enabling more homes to save money on their electricity bills and earn revenue through the smart export guarantee as well as reducing their carbon footprint., We believe the current grid and way we use energy is unsustainable. One way of addressing this is by reducing reliance on the grid. This is where Solar PV and battery will help. Spending now on reducing the reliance on the grid will save countless billions on upgrades.

Stop the plans to allow schools to drop poetry from the GCSE syllabus, Retain the current status of poetry in the GCSE syllabus, Our young need the creative outlet of poetry to express their passions and emotions. With the rising number of suicides among the young do not underplay this important means of expression. Please keep its status in our children's programme of study or else we will see their lives diminish and become placid and lifeless.

Unleash this nation of entrepreneurs by transforming Start Up funding, Transform the Start Up Loan scheme to be more like student loans, but for entrepreneurs: Government-backed, low interest, unsecured loans available to anyone, at any age, who wants to start a business. Like a student loan, the entrepreneur loan only becomes repayable when you earn enough. , The number one barrier to starting a business is lack of money. Ordinary working people cannot risk quitting their jobs, defaulting on mortgages, and plunging their family into poverty in order to pursue their aspirations. We are a nation of creative entrepreneurs at heart. Yet so much of that talent is wasted. We need to uncork that energy and offer everyone, no-matter their walk of life, the opportunity to build something incredible. It is a national economic imperative. It's social mobility for a generation and rocket fuel for our economy.

Provide financial assistance to those prohibited from giving facial treatments, Provide financial support, incentives, similar to the eat out to help out scheme, or bail outs, such as those given to the arts, to professionals within the beauty industry, currently prohibited from carrying out facial treatments. The beauty industry generated 2.7billion for the UK economy in 2017., The public has been incentivised to go out and eat. The arts have been allocated £1.6 billion bailout. The beauty industry is forced to operate without being able to offer their most profitable and popular treatments. The industry comprises mainly of female entrepreneurs, 94% of those working in beauty are female. Research shows that when women earn money, they spend it on their family,  improving quality of life for others.

Extend rights to Paid Statutory Bereavement Leave, I would like UK Government to pass legislation creating a right to Paid Statutory Bereavement Leave following the death of any dependants, including parents., Currently there is only statutory bereavement pay and leave - for two weeks - for parents whose child dies under the age of 18, or certain cases of losing a pregnancy.

Employees can take time off to deal with an emergency involving a dependent, but this does not have to be paid and is insufficient for bereaved family members.

The UK Government needs to implement a paid statutory bereavement policy in order that families can mourn and heal after loss, without added financial stress.

Reverse the change to Small Brewers Relief., The Treasury has announced changes to Small Brewers Relief (SBR) – the progressive tax system that has revolutionised UK brewing. These changes will reduce the 50% duty threshold from 5,000hl to 2,100hl: small breweries will have to pay more duty, whilst larger breweries could pay the same or less., Those that will have to pay more do not know by how much as the consultation has been delayed until the Autumn. This is creating grave uncertainty for many small breweries at a time when the industry is trying to survive the Covid-19 crisis.

We believe the Treasury should not reduce relief for any brewers below 5,000hl and should reverse its decision to reduce the threshold to 2,100hl, and that these changes are threatening closures, innovation, competition, local jobs, investment and consumer choice.

Child Maintenance Service should Charge Self employed parents the same as PAYE., Self employed parents have no action taken against them when they miss weekly child maintenance payments or when there is a debt, additionally funds are not being taken direct. Self employed parents are also paying incorrect, lower weekly amounts. The HMRC should be working alongside the child maintenance service to ensure self employed parents are paying the correct weekly amount to their child and any debts should be taken from the paying parents annual rebate. Why are these parents legally not paying.

Change method to work out child maintenance to be based on net not gross income, Change the method for calculating child maintenance payments by the paying parent to be based on net income not gross income and do not add on values such as company car benefit in kind  as this is not actual income!, My CMS total payments amount to 23% of my net income. Life is very difficult as I must also support my daughter at Uni who does not qualify for the full loans to live. I’m expected to add £6k a year to help her whilst supporting my son who chooses to live full time with his dad at £8400 a year . I’m completely broke. I earn a decent salary but I feel penalised for earning well and having a company car and my daughter does not qualify for a full maintenance loan and has to apply for hardship grants

Support the culture sector by launching a “Visit a Theatre, To Help Out” scheme, We’re calling on Government to launch a “Visit a Theatre, To Help Out” scheme similar to the initiative that has helped the hospitality sector. Socially-distanced audiences are not a viable business model for many theatres - who face massive loss of income. 

Many theatres have cancelled their pantomime, which generates a large proportion of their annual income. 

By launching a subsidised ticket scheme on Monday-Wednesday performances, the Government could both kickstart the theatre sector but also boost economic activity in towns across the UK.

Formally classify unpaid carers as "workers" of the state, under the law., We the undersigned want the UK Parliament to pass legislation formally classifying unpaid carers as "workers" under UK law, just like their private and public sector counterparts and give them the same rights as any other worker., Unpaid carers are required under UK law to provide care for a minimum of 35 hours per week (most work over 60). This is a term of employment. Carers working 60 hours per week receive on average £2.30 per hour. This is not acceptably. The way the UK treats carers is exploitation, affording them no workers rights at all, as valued members of the workforce who save the UK £135 billion per year, equivelant to the budgets for the NHS in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland combined.

Send aid to Mauritius to help clear the oil spill., The UK has experienced oil spills in the past and know the catastrophic effects that it can cause to the biodiversity of native wildlife. Resources within Mauritius to clear an oil spill of this size are limited and, therefore, aiding the country to clear the spill is essential., From our history of oil spills, such as the Torrey Canyon disaster in 1967 spilling 119,000 tonnes of crude oil, we are able to provide expertise, equipment and solutions to the communities who are working to contain and clear the oil spill. This is needed to be done sooner rather than later due to the disastrous effects it can cause on the environment as well as the country’s economy that strongly relies on tourism, due to its pristine coasts.

Help out of school and extra-curricular club providers bounce back from Covid-19, #ClubTogether - An initiative supported by central government to offer financial assistance to struggling, out of school and extra-curricular activity providers severely impacted by Covid-19. Much like the ‘Eat out to help out’ scheme, parents and children need help to return to sport safely., The fallout from Covid-19 on children’s health and fitness cannot be understated. With guidance unclear and schools and vendors making their own decisions on how and when to bring clubs and sport back, companies and individuals offering activities for children in these settings are at risk of complete financial ruin. I want government to agree to either partially subsidise (up to 50% and no more than £25 per child) spaces for children or request schools fund this via their sports budget.

Introduce statutory rates of pay and allowances for HGV drivers, We want statutory rates of pay and allowances for HGV drivers that ensure:

- Night out allowance should be raised to £45 minimum
- Drivers who complete a 10-hour shift should get a £10 meal allowance, raised to £15 if nighting out, Many HGV drivers work long hours sometimes with little rest between shifts and working weeks, and also face the costs of having to pay premium prices for roadside food and drink.
 
HGV drivers perform an essential service, and the Government should recognise this by introducing statutory rates of pay and allowances, so that HGV drivers are reimbursed for their work and expenses appropriately.

A LEVEL RESULTS 2020. REVERSE THE DECISION OF DOWNGRADING RESULTS., Reverse the decision made to down grade A Level results. Adhere to the predicted grades offered by schools/colleges and the professionals that know their students. One year only., Unfair.

Make the Eat Out To Help Out scheme an annual event, The government should make the Eat Out to Help Out scheme a yearly event happening every August. It has also provided the whole nation a sense of unity and joy in a very depressing year. Our resilience in 2020 should be celebrated every year through this scheme. Furthoremore, in a world becoming more and more digital, it is a great incentive to boost the local economies during the summer. The scheme has already seen more than 10.5m meals claimed.

Financial support for those who become self employed during 2019-2020 tax year, Many self employed are entitled to grants and pay back loans all across the UK, but there is nothing for those who registered their business during the 2019-2020 tax year. Many people go self employed or set up their businesses every year and are affected by the eligibility criteria set in place!, There has to be some help out there for those who are new businesses and have had or still don't have no work or income due to the pandemic we are in. Universal credit and such benefits disregarded. The self employed who started there businesses after April 2019 need help too!

Start to take into account 2019-2020 income for self employed new businesses! We have lives too and are being completely disregarded in the financial self employment scheme!

Extend the eat out help out scheme at least until end of September., Please extend the eat out help out scheme at least until end of September.
Encourage the restaurants to open the whole week and hire staff full time., As I work in industry and can see the difference day by day, the eat out help out scheme really helped the restaurant businesses to start recovering. But what happens when this is going to end on 31st of August?  Monday to Wednesday feels like 2nd weekend and restaurants have been busier than ever. 
Extending the scheme until end of September will encourage restaurants to open full time and start hiring.That means even more people will be going out to eat. Some people are finding out about the scheme now, on 3rd week. 
The food suppliers have started recovering too as well as the farmers, bakers, fishermen etc.
If the scheme will end, probably many restaurants will be closed again these 3 days and work part time.

Fully re-open the Office for National Insurance Immediately, The Office for National Insurance was closed due to Covid for a number of months. Fully re-open this office to allow all those who need an NI number to obtain one., This comes about as my Irish fiancée is looking to come to the UK to live, work and marry; as a mental health professional, you would think they would be required at this time. It is impossible for many to obtain an NI number however whilst this office is providing such limited service. This affects all applicants from other countries, and can bar them from working and paying the right amount of tax and will result in a backlog of rebates in the future.

Make Free School Meals (FSM) fairer and accessible to ALL low income families, The Government should extend the free school meals scheme to include the provision of food vouchers for low income families who have to provide a packed lunch for their child, due to dietary, sensory or educational needs as well as those who home school. , If parents are entitled to help why should they suffer financially because child has sensory/dietary needs and can’t access FSM.
 
Also many families due to having children with additional needs/no suitable school places, home educate their children. In recent years a large number of parents who home educate are low income families where Home Education is the best option for the child but the parents, struggle financially.

Allow Notice Pay to be tax exempt for those receiving zero redundancy pay., Due to Covid 19, many are being made redundant with zero statutory redundancy pay. Extend furlough beyond October for the travel industry., Consider extending the furlough scheme for those industries still being affected. Front line security workers to receive perm key worker status and benefits, To ensure front line security professionals recieve key worker status and benefits permanently and receive recognition as a professional industry., We need the Government to recognise the security industry and support its hard working staff. Extend the furlough scheme for all the furlough workers till the next year 2021., We call on the Government to keep furlough scheme going beyond October. Review need for social distancing inside theatres before November, Given the dire situation the theatre industry is in we call on the Government to review the continued imposition of social distancing in indoor theatres as soon as possible (and on a regular basis thereafter should it need to remain in force) and well before the currently stated timeline of November, The theatre industry is benefiting from the culture bail-out but that sum cannot do more than help some venues and organisations survive the current closure. Give unpaid carers the same benefits as those on other allowance based benefits, To give those unpaid carers who care for loved ones in receipt of carers allowance the same benefits as those on other allowance based benefits, such as free prescriptions, free dental care and free optician appointments and help paying for glasses, For those unpaid carers who care for loved ones, and receive carers allowance, like those on other allowance based benefits unpaid carers are only allowed to earn £128 and work up to 16 hours a week, yet despite having the same restrictions placed on the amount they can earn and work, they are not in receipt of the same benefits when it comes to health care with dentists, opticians and prescriptions, carers allowance is no where near enough to cover the ever rising costs of day to day life.

End the practice of Payments on Account for self-employed, HMRC should end the practice of payments on account for self-employed people., The practice is putting some small businesses and sole traders into a position where advanced payments towards their tax bill cannot be made. Protect the UK's dwindling hedgehog population before it's too late., Now the hedgehog has been listed as vulnerable to extinction in the UK, we are calling on the Government to move hedgehogs to schedule 5 of the Wildlife & Countryside Act 1981 to allow them greater protection., This change will mean hedgehogs will be afforded greater protection and hopefully help their numbers recover.

Low or interest free loans for leaseholders affected by cladding regs and EWS1., To enable leaseholders to make their homes safe the government should offer a similar “up scaled” loan package as the Covid 19 bounce back loan scheme. Extend the Furlough Scheme past the 31st of October, We want the furloughing scheme to be extended past the 31st of October 2020 to at least the 31st of February 2021, extending it by an extra four months., The reason for this is not only because this provides needed clarity to businesses, especially small ones that were already entering a risky environment financially (even before COVID) but also to help those that would otherwise be unemployed.

Exclude children under 12 months from the social distancing rules in England, Exclude children under 12 months from the social distancing rules restricting groups to no more than 6 people. A public enquiry into the financial dealings of Warrington Borough Council, Warrington borough council’s borrowing has risen in a very short space of time from a few hundred thousand to now over £1.6 billion. Exempt children from "Rule of 6" England., Exempt children from "Rule of 6" England., As a family of 6 who have stuck to all the lockdown rules we are now being penalised  for being a large family, or having children at all. Extend furlough for restricted sectors, Please extend the furlough scheme in restricted sectors to protect jobs and make sure the businesses can get up and running as quickly as possible once restrictions are fully lifted., The current arrangement for furlough is not taking into account the asymmetric nature of the businesses that are still affected by the virus and will be unable to open in any meaningful way by the end of October. Change Universal Credit to payments every 4 weeks, I want the broken and failing universal credit payment calendar to change. Change the payment calendar to 4 weekly instead of monthly, as at the moment extra payments in a month can make you lose entitlement. This month of zero UC isn't helping anyone it's meant to instead it creates or deepens poverty. Fix this broken system for once and all.

Make the national insurance rate 12% universal on money earned., I believe that those who earn over £962 a week should pay 12% and not have it reduced to 2% on the rest of their earnings due to the fact that the coronavirus can only be treated by the NHS and no private health insurance can cope with it., The debate will make more people aware of this reduced rate (the Upper Earnings  Limit) and Government will have to explain why those who are in the top 10% of earners are getting this lower rate while the rest of the UK'S workforce have to pay the full amount on what they earn.

Extend business rates holiday for retail & hospitality businesses, There is an urgent need to reform the current business rates, however rate reform being postponed. Extend the Furlough scheme to hospitality employees effected by local lockdowns, We are calling for the government to extend the furlough scheme to hospitality industries effected hugely by local lockdowns. Calls on the government to extend furlough beyond 31st October 2020., We call on the government to extend Furlough and protect workers., With Covid 19 still very much on the rise and the potential for another lockdown.Many UK citizens are worried for their job security.Without an extension to Furlough the impact on workers and business will be devastating.

Provide financial support to the hospitality industry who is unable to open, 1)Extend furlough for the duration of time nightclubs, theatres, events are closed/cancelled

Create a Minister for Hospitality in the UK Government, The UK hospitality industry. Responsible for around 3m jobs, generating £130bn in activity, resulting in £38bn in taxation. Yet, unlike the Arts or Sports, we do not have a dedicated Minister.

Allow businesses to top up Bounce Back Loans (BBLs), It is now time for these loan schemes to be extended to allow 'top ups' for businesses who are continuing to face difficulty. Do not supplement the Sovereign Grant, It has been reported in the Daily Mail that the Treasury is planning to put more tax payer money into the Sovereign Grant to make up for the Queen's land and property investments not making as much money as expected due to the Covid situation. Pay musicians for lost income from contracted guaranteed fees due to Covid-19, Government should help musicians who rely on contracted guaranteed fees by paying lost income for all full agreed fees to artists amidst the Coronavirus restrictions., Myself and many colleagues and friends have lost their entire income due to the restrictions that prevent us from working. Remove the 50% Self Employed Rule for those with a P45 dated before UK Lockdown, The SEISS requires trading profits to be at least equal to non-trading income. This is 'to ensure it is targeted at those who are most reliant on self-employment income.'

Give a one off £12k grant to all those excluded from both SEISS & CJRS, Give a one off grant to all those who have been unable to access both SEISS and CJRS and who have either a UTR or were PAYE in 2020, Because leaving people behind the rest of the country is immoral

advance of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)

Hospitality

Allocated time for fireworks to be set off on 5th November., Created an allocated time from 18:00 to 20:00 on 5th November where fireworks are allowed to be set off., People with disabilities, pets, and families often find 5th November - bonfire night, one of the most distressing times of the year. The Government must contribute NI and Pensions under the new furlough scheme., The Government should cover NI and pensions contributions under the extended furlough scheme from November, as in the original scheme earlier this year. Do not delay the Job Retention Bonus: businesses are relying on this money, When furlough was extended to March the Government also announced the Job Retention Bonus would no longer be paid in February. More financial support for long covid sufferers, Long covid sufferers get no financial support, we dont get 80 percent of wages, we get no financial help at all and its us that is suffering!. Change the bounce back loan turnover from 25% to 50%, I would like the government to change the criteria for the bounce back loan, as I have spoke to a lot of people and they underestimated their annual turnover due to the uncertainty from this pandemic. Additional Funding for Local and Community Theatres during the COVID-19 Pandemic, At least 30% of Local & Community Theatres are on the verge of total collapse and will permanently close by March 2021. Extend income replacement schemes to those who don't currently qualify, To address the gaping holes in the self-employed income support scheme (SEISS) and extend support to the desperately struggling newly self-employed, limited company directors and other groups that have been left devastated after seven months with no support., The first lockdown came into force on the 23 of March 2020 leaving many unable to get their tax return in before the cut-off point of 23 April, meaning they were ineligible for financial support.

Spend the additional £16.5bn in defence spending in public services instead, The Government have recently announced they are spending an additional £16.5bn in defence spending.
